To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RNA regulons can be dysregulated in cancer to drive oncogenic phenotypes.

1) RNA regulon model provides a framework for understanding how cancer cell phenotypes are driven by coordinated regulation of mRNAs encoding proteins in the biochemical pathways; 2) RNA regulons are dysregulated in many cancers and this can lead to altered protein expression and cancer cell phenotypes; 3) RNA regulons can be exploited for cancer diagnosis and treatment.

1) the RNA regulon concept can help explain the coordination of mRNA processing in cancer; 2) dysregulation of RNA metabolism can underlie cancer phenotypes and 3) RNA regulons may represent novel targets to treat cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of post-transcriptional regulation on the cell and how this can be exploited in cancer.

understanding the mechanisms of RNA metabolism and how these are co-opted by cancer cells to drive their oncogenic programs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RNA regulon hypothesis provides a powerful framework for understanding the impact of RNA regulation in the context of human disease.
post-transcriptional regulation is a critical determinant of cellular phenotype and cancer biology.
the post-transcriptional regulatory networks in cancer cells are altered, and these alterations have a direct and significant impact on the cancer cell phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cancer is a disease driven by dysregulated RNA metabolism.
cancer cells are not simply driven by a handful of genetic mutations, but instead are the result of a complex interplay of genetic mutations, epigenetic and post-transcriptional changes.
post-transcriptional regulation is important for cancer and that the dysregulation of RNA regulons can drive the phenotypes we observe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dysregulation of mRNA processing pathways can have a profound impact on cancer cell biology and that this is an underappreciated area of research in the cancer field.
RNA processing events are important drivers of oncogenesis.
post-transcriptional regulation of mRNAs can have profound consequences for the cancer cell phenotype and that this dysregulation is a major driver of the disease.
